verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              द्विवर्षोपनिवृत्तेषु पाण्डवेषु यदृच्छया। देवर्षिर्नारदो राजन्नाजगाम युधिष्ठिरम्॥१॥
verses.english: After two years had passed from the date of the return of the Pandavas from the retreat of heir sire), the celestial Rishi, Narada, O king, came to Yudhishthria.

verses.sanskrit: तमभ्यर्च्य महाबाहुः कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः। आसीनं परिविश्वस्तं प्रोवाच वदतां वरः॥२॥
चिरात्तु नानुपश्यामि भगवन्तमुपस्थितम्। कच्चित्ते कुशलं विप्र शुभं वा प्रत्युपस्थितम्॥३॥
verses.english: the mighty-armed Kuru king, that foremost of speakers, viz., Yudhishthira, having duly adored him, made him take a seat. After the Rishi had rested a while, the king asked him saying, 'It is after a long time that I see your holy self arrived at my court. Are you in peace and happiness, O learned Bhimasena?

verses.sanskrit: के देशाः परिदृष्टास्ते किं च कार्यं करोमि ते। तद्ब्रूहि द्विजमुख्यस्त्वं त्वं ह्यस्माकं परा गतिः॥४॥
verses.english: What are toe countries which you have passed through? What can I do for you? Do you tell me. You are the foremost of twiceborn ones, and you are our highest refuge.

verses.sanskrit:
नारद उवाच।
              चिरदृष्टोऽसि मेत्येवमागतोऽहं तपोवनात्। परिदृष्टानि तीर्थानि गङ्गा चैव मया नृप॥५॥

युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              वदन्ति पुरुषा मेऽद्य गङ्गातीरनिवासिनः। धृतराष्ट्रं महात्मानमास्थितं परमं तपः॥६॥
अपि दृष्टस्त्वया तत्र कुशली स कुरूद्वहः। गान्धारी च पृथा चैव सूतपुत्रश्च सञ्जयः॥७॥
verses.english: Have you seen him there? Is that perpetuator o Kuru's race in peace? Are Gandhari and Pritha and the Suta's son Sanjaya also in peace?

verses.sanskrit: कथं च वर्तते चाद्य पिता मम स पार्थिवः। श्रोतुमिच्छामि भगवन्यदि दृष्टस्त्वया नृपः॥८॥
verses.english: How, indeed, is that royal sire of mine doing? I wish to hear this, O holy one, if you have seen the king.

verses.sanskrit:
नारद उवाच।
              स्थिरीभूय महाराज शृणु वृत्तं यथातथम्। यथा श्रुतं च दृष्टं च मया तस्मिंस्तपोवने॥९॥
verses.english: Narada said Listen, O king, with calmness to me as I tell you what I have heard and seen in that asylum.

verses.sanskrit: वनवासनिवृत्तेषु भवत्सु कुरुनन्दन। कुरुक्षेत्रात्पिता तुभ्यं गङ्गाद्वारं ययौ नृप॥१०॥
verses.english: After your return from Kurukshetra, O delighter of the Kurus, Your sire, O king, proceeded towards Gangadvara.

verses.sanskrit: गान्धार्या सहितो धीमान् वध्वा कुन्त्या समन्वितः। सञ्जयेन च सूतेन साग्निहोज्ञः सयाजकः॥११॥
verses.english: That intelligent king took with him his (sacred) fire, Gandhari and his daughter-in-law Kunti, as also Sanjaya of the Suta caste, and all the Yajakas.

verses.sanskrit: आतस्थे स तपस्तीव्रं पिता तव तपोधनः। वीटां मुखे समाधाय वायुभक्षोऽभवन्मुनिः॥१२॥
वने स मुनिभिः सर्वैः पूज्यमानो महातपाः। त्वगस्थिमात्रशेषः स षण्मासानभवन्नृपः॥१३॥
verses.english: Engaged in severe penances, he was adored by all the ascetics in the forest. In six months the king was reduced to only a skeleton.

verses.sanskrit: गान्धारी तु जलाहारी कुन्ती मासोपवासिनी। सञ्जयः षष्ठभुक्तेन वर्तयामास भारत॥१४॥
verses.english: Gandhari lived on water alone, while Kunti took a little food a intervals of month. Sanjaya, O Bharata, lived, eating a little every sixth day.

verses.sanskrit: अग्नींस्तु याजकास्तत्र जुहुवुर्विधिवत्प्रभो। दृश्यतोऽदृश्यतश्चैव वने तस्मिन्नृपस्य वै॥१५॥
अनिकेतोऽथ राजा स बभूव वनगोचरः। ते चापि सहिते देव्यौ सञ्जयश्च तमन्वयुः॥१६॥
verses.english: The king had no fixed dwelling. He became a wanderer through those forests. The two queens, as also Sanjaya, followed him.
verses.bhavadeepa: दृश्यतोऽदृश्यत इति पश्यन्तमपश्यन्तं चानादृत्यर्थः। नियमेन सान्निध्याभावात्॥१५॥

verses.sanskrit: सञ्जयो नृपतेर्नेता समेषु विषमेषु च। गान्धार्याश्च पृथा चैव चक्षुरासीदनिन्दिता॥१७॥
verses.english: Sanjaya acted as the guide on even and uneven land. The faultless Pritha, O king, became the eye of Gandhari.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कदाचिद्गङ्गायाः कच्छे स नृपसत्तमः। गङ्गायामाप्लुतो धीमानाश्रमाभिमुखोऽभवत्॥१८॥
verses.english: One day, that best of kings went to a spot on the margin of Ganga. He then bathed in the sacred river and finishing his ablutions turned his face toward his hermitage.

verses.sanskrit: अथ वायुः समुद्भूतो दावाग्निरभवन्महान्। ददाह तद्वनं सर्वं परिगृह्य समन्वतः॥१९॥
verses.english: The wind rose high. A fierce wild fire set in. It began to burn that forest all around.

verses.sanskrit: दह्यत्सु मृगयूथेषु द्विजिह्वेषु समन्ततः। वराहाणां च यूथेषु संश्रयत्सु जलाशयान्॥२०॥
verses.english: When the herds of animals were being burnt all around, as also the snakes which inhabited. that region, herds of wild board began to take themselves to the nearest marshes and waters.

verses.sanskrit: समाविद्धे वने तस्मिन्प्राप्ते व्यसन उत्तमे। निराहारतया राजन्मन्दप्राणविचेष्टितः॥२१॥
verses.english: When that forest was thus afflicted on all sides and such distress came upon all the living creature living there, the king, who had taken no food, was incapable of moving or exerting himself at all.

verses.sanskrit: असमर्थोऽपसरणे सुकृशे मातरौ च ते। ततः स नृपतिर्दृष्ट्वा वह्निमायान्तमन्तिकात्॥२२॥
verses.english: Your two mothers also, exceedingly emaciated, could not move. The king, seeing the fire approach him from all sides, addressed the Suta Sanjaya, that foremost of skillful charioteers, saying, 'Go, O Sanjaya, to such a place where the fire may not burn you.

verses.sanskrit: इदमाह ततः सूतं सञ्जयं जयतां वरः। गच्छ सञ्जय यत्राग्निर्न त्वां दहति कर्हिचित्॥२३॥
वयमत्राग्निना युक्ता गमिष्यामः परां गतिम्। तमुवाच किलोद्विग्नः सञ्जयो वदतां वरः॥२४॥
verses.english: As regards ourselves, we shall allow our bodies to be destroyed by this fire and attain to the greatest end. To him, Sanjaya, that foremost of speakers, said-'O king, this death, brought on by a fire that is not sacred, will prove calamitous to you. I do not, however, see any means by which you can escape from this fire. our

verses.sanskrit: राजन्मृत्युरनिष्टोऽयं भविता ते वृथाग्निना। न चोपाय प्रपश्यामि मोक्षणे जातवेदसः॥२५॥
यदत्रानन्तरं कार्यं तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति। इत्युक्तः सञ्जयेनेदं पुनराह स पार्थिवः॥२६॥
verses.english: That which should next be done should be marked by you. Thus addressed by Sanjaya the king once more said, “This death cannot be calamitous to us, for we have left our home of own accord. Water, fire, wind, and abstention from food, are laudable for ascetics. Do you, therefore, leave us, O Sanjaya, forthwith.' Having said these words to Sanjaya the king concentrated his mind.

verses.sanskrit: नैष मृत्युरनिष्टो नो निःसृतानां गृहात्स्वयम्। जलमग्निस्तथा वायुरथवाऽपि विकर्षणम्॥२७॥
तापसानां प्रशस्यन्ते गच्छ सञ्जय माचिरम्। इत्युक्त्वा सञ्जयं राजा समाधाय मनस्तथा॥२८॥
प्राङ्मुखः सह गान्धार्या कुन्त्या चोपाविशत्तदा। सञ्जयस्तं तथा दृष्ट्वा प्रदक्षिणमथाकरोत्॥२९॥
verses.english: Facing the east, he sat down, with Gandhari and Kunti. Seeing him in that attitude Sanjaya walked round him.

verses.sanskrit: उवाच चैनं मेधावी युड्क्ष्वात्मानमिति प्रभो। ऋषिपुत्रो मनीषी स राजा चक्रेऽस्य तद्वचः॥३०॥
verses.english: Gifted with intelligence, Sanjaya said, 'Do you concentrate your mind. O powerful one!' The son of a Rishi, and himself endued with great wisdom, the king acted as he was told.

verses.sanskrit: सन्निमध्येन्द्रियग्राममासीत्काष्ठोपमस्तदा। गान्धारी च महाभागा जननी च पृथा तव॥३१॥
verses.english: Governing all the senses, he remained like a post of wood. The highly blessed Gandhari, and your mother Pritha top, remained in the same attitude.

verses.sanskrit: दावाग्निना समायुक्ते स च राजा पिता तव। सञ्जयस्तु महामात्रस्तस्माद्दावादमुच्यत॥३२॥
verses.english: Then your royal sire was overtaken by the wild-fire, Sanjaya, his minister succeeded in escaping from that fire.

verses.sanskrit: गङ्गाकूले मया दृष्टस्तापसैः परिवारितः। स तानामन्त्र्य तेजस्वी निवेद्येतच्च सर्वशः॥३३॥
verses.english: I saw him on the banks of Ganga in the midst of ascetics. Gifted with great, energy and great intelligence's he bade them farewell and then started for the mountains of Himavat.

verses.sanskrit: प्रययौ सञ्जयो धीमान् हिमवन्तं महीधरम्। एवं स निधनं प्राप्तः कुरुराजो महामनाः॥३४॥
गान्धारी च पृथा चैव जनन्यौ ते विशाम्पते। यदृच्छयानुव्रजता मया राज्ञः कलेवरम्॥३५॥
verses.english: Thus the great Kuru king met with his death, and it was thus that Gandhari and Kunti, your two others, also met with death, O monarch.

verses.sanskrit: तयोश्च देव्योरुभयोर्मया दृष्टानि भारत। ततस्तपोवने तस्मिन् समाजग्मुस्तपोधनाः॥३६॥
verses.english: In course of my wanderings at will, I saw the bodies of that king and those two queens, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा राज्ञस्तदा निष्ठां न त्वशोचन् गतीश्च ते। तत्राश्रौषमहं सर्वमेतत्पुरुषसत्तम॥३७॥
verses.english: Many ascetics came to that asylum, having heard of the end of king Dhritarashtra. They did not at all grieve for that end of theirs.

verses.sanskrit: यथा च नृपतिर्दग्धो देव्यौ ते चेति पाण्डव। न शोचितव्यं राजेन्द्र स्वतः स पृथिवीपतिः॥३८॥
verses.english: There, O best of men, I heard all the details of how the king and the two qucens, O son of Pandu, had been burnt.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राप्तवानग्निसंयोगं गान्धारी जननी च ते।
              वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतच्छ्रुत्वा च सर्वेषां पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्॥३९॥
verses.english: O king of kings, you should not grieve for him. The monarch, of his own will, as also Gandhari and your mother, got that contact with fire,

verses.sanskrit: निर्याणं धृतराष्ट्रस्य शोकः समभवन्महान्। अन्तःपुराणां च तदा महानार्तस्वरोऽभवत्॥४०॥
verses.english: Lord sounds of wailing were heard within the inner apartments of the palace. The citizens also, hearing of the end of the old king, bewailed aloud.

verses.sanskrit: अहो धिगिति राजा तु विक्रुश्य भृशदुःखितः॥४१॥
verses.english: 'O Fie', cried king Yudhishthira in great agony, raising his arms a loft. Thinking of his mother, he wept like a child. All is brothers too, headed by Bhimasena, old the same.

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वबाहुः स्मरन्मातुः प्ररुरोद युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनपुरोगाश्च भ्रातरः सर्व एव ते॥४२॥
अन्तःपुरेषु च तदा सुमहान् रुदितस्वनः। प्रादुरासीन्महाराज पृथां श्रुत्वा तथागताम्॥४३॥
verses.english: Hearing that Pritha had met with such a face, the royal ladies bewailed aloud in grief.

verses.sanskrit: तं च वृद्धं तथा दग्धं हतपुत्रं नराधिपम्। अन्वशोचन्त ते सर्वे गान्धारीं च तपस्विनीम्॥४४॥
तस्मिन्नुपरते शब्दे मुहूर्तादिव भारत। निगृह्य बाष्पं धैर्येण धर्मराजोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥४५॥
verses.english: When those sounds of wailing ceased for a while, king Yudhishthira the just, shopping his tears by summoning all his patience, said these words.
